title: Star motif — five point
subtitle: A flat five-pointed star worked in the round with treble spikes radiating from the centre
excerpt: Five treble spike sections radiate from the magic ring, each separated by a chain-2 indentation to cut the star shape into the fabric. Three rounds give a 10 cm star with sharp points suitable for applique, bunting, and blanket squares.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1888), five-point star motif chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A five-point crochet star motif in golden yellow DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Sharp points, flat centre, no holes between the spike sections, 10 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished five-point star measures 10 cm tip to tip in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Star motif — five point
chartDefinition.caption: Five spike sections separated by ch-2 indentations. Each spike grows taller toward the tip and tapers back through decreases.

glossaryTerms.definition: The chain-2 space at the valley between star points. Working a slip stitch into this space pulls the fabric inward, sharpening the angle between each point.

content.text: The five-point star builds each point by stepping up from double crochet to half treble to treble — taller stitches at the tip — then stepping back down. The
between each point is a chain-2 space with a slip stitch pulled through it on the border round, pulling the valley sharp.

The star lies flat only after a firm steam-block with the points pinned. Before blocking it cups slightly at the indentations — that is normal. Pin each tip and valley to the blocking mat and leave overnight.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Blocking mat and pins essential for sharp points.

content.text: Magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 4 tr into ring. *Ch 2, 5 tr into ring.* Rep 4 more times. Ch 2. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. Pull ring closed. (25 tr, 5 ch-2 valleys.)
Sl st along to first tr of a 5-tr section. *2 dc, 1 htr, 1 tr, ch 2 (tip), 1 tr, 1 htr, 2 dc. Sl st into ch-2 valley.* Rep from * around all 5 sections.
Work dc around each point edge: *3 dc up one side of point. Ch 1 at tip. 3 dc down the other side. Sl st into valley.* Rep from * around. Fasten off.
Work the eight-point star for a more complex star shape with additional points. Or try the compass rose round for a circular motif with pointed sections.
